sentences.en: I am a writer. Writing books is my profession but it's more than that, of course.
sentences.zh: 我是个作家 写书是我的职业

sentences.en: It is also my great lifelong love and fascination.
sentences.zh: 这也是我一生深爱和迷恋

sentences.en: And I don't expect that that's ever going to change.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那会改变

sentences.en: But, that said, something kind of peculiar has happened recently in my life and in my career, which has caused me to have to recalibrate my whole relationship with this work.
sentences.zh: 但是,说到这里,最近我的生活和事业中发生了一些奇怪的事情,这导致我不得不重新调整我与这项工作的整个关系。

sentences.en: And the peculiar thing is that I recently wrote this book, this memoir called "Eat, Pray, Love" which, decidedly unlike any of my previous books, went out in the world for some reason, and became this big,
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是,我最近写了这本书, 这个回忆录叫做"吃,祈祷,爱", 与我以前的任何一本书不同,

sentences.en: mega-sensation, international bestseller thing.
sentences.zh: 超感应,国际畅销书

sentences.en: The result of which is that everywhere I go now, people treat me like I'm doomed.
sentences.zh: 结果是现在我走到哪里 人们都把我当成注定要死的人一样对待

sentences.en: Seriously -- doomed, doomed! Like, they come up to me now, all worried, and they say, "Aren't you afraid you're never going to be able to top that?
sentences.zh: 说真的 注定要失败 注定要失败

sentences.en: Aren't you afraid you're going to keep writing for your whole life and you're never again going to create a book that anybody in the world cares about at all, ever again?"
sentences.zh: 难道你不害怕你 继续写你的整个生活 你永远不会再次 创造一本书 世界上的任何人 关心的, 永远不再?"

sentences.en: So that's reassuring, you know. But it would be worse, except for that I happen to remember that over 20 years ago, when I was a teenager, when I first started telling people that I wanted to be a writer, I was met with this same sort of fear-based reaction.
sentences.zh: 所以,这是令人欣慰的,你知道的。但情况会更糟, 除了我恰好记得20多年前,当我还是一个青少年的时候, 当我开始告诉人们我想成为一个作家的时候, 我遇到了同样的恐惧反应。

sentences.en: And people would say, "Aren't you afraid you're never going to have any success?
sentences.zh: 人们会说,"你不担心你永远不会成功吗?

sentences.en: Aren't you afraid the humiliation of rejection will kill you?
sentences.zh: 你不怕被排斥的羞辱会杀了你吗?

sentences.en: Aren't you afraid that you're going to work your whole life at this craft and nothing's ever going to come of it and you're going to die on a scrap heap of broken dreams with your mouth filled with bitter ash of failure?"
sentences.zh: 难道你不害怕 你要去工作 你的整个生活 在这个手工艺品 和没有什么会从它来 你会死 在一堆碎碎的梦 用你的嘴充满苦灰 失败?"

sentences.en: (Laughter) Like that, you know. The answer -- the short answer to all those questions is, "Yes."
sentences.zh: 就像那样,你知道的。答案是,所有这些问题的简短答案是,“是的”。

sentences.en: Yes, I'm afraid of all those things. And I always have been.
sentences.zh: 是的,我怕那些东西,我一直都是

sentences.en: And I'm afraid of many, many more things besides that people can't even guess at, like seaweed and other things that are scary.
sentences.zh: 我害怕很多, 更多的事情 除了人们甚至无法猜到, 像海藻和其他可怕的事情。

sentences.en: But, when it comes to writing, the thing that I've been sort of thinking about lately, and wondering about lately, is why?
sentences.zh: 但是,在写作方面, 我最近一直在想的事情, 并且最近一直在想, 为什么呢?

sentences.en: You know, is it rational? Is it logical that anybody should be expected to be afraid of the work that they feel they were put on this Earth to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道,这是理性的吗?合乎逻辑的是,谁应该害怕他们感到自己被投入地球的工作。

sentences.en: And what is it specifically about creative ventures that seems to make us really nervous about each other's mental health in a way that other careers kind of don't do, you know?
sentences.zh: 具体地说,创意企业 似乎让我们对对方的心理健康 感到非常紧张, 而其他职业却并不如此,你知道吗?

sentences.en: Like my dad, for example, was a chemical engineer and I don't recall once in his 40 years of chemical engineering anybody asking him if he was afraid to be a chemical engineer, you know?
sentences.zh: 比如说 我爸爸是个化学工程师 我不记得他40年的化学工程 曾经有人问他 是否害怕当化学工程师

sentences.en: "That chemical-engineering block, John, how's it going?"
sentences.zh: "那个化学工程块,约翰,怎么样?"

sentences.en: It just didn't come up like that, you know?
sentences.zh: 它只是没有 出这样的,你知道吗?

sentences.en: But to be fair, chemical engineers as a group haven't really earned a reputation over the centuries for being alcoholic manic-depressives.
sentences.zh: 但公平地说, 化学工程师作为一个团体 并没有真正赢得一个声誉 在几个世纪以来 酗酒的躁郁症。

sentences.en: (Laughter) We writers, we kind of do have that reputation, and not just writers, but creative people across all genres, it seems, have this reputation for being enormously mentally unstable.
sentences.zh: 我们作家,我们确实有这样的名声, 不只是作家, 和创造性的人 在所有类型, 它似乎,有这样的名声 极不稳定的精神。

sentences.en: And all you have to do is look at the very grim death count in the 20th century alone, of really magnificent creative minds who died young and often at their own hands, you know?
sentences.zh: 你要做的就是看20世纪最可怕的死亡数字, 仅仅看那些年轻、常常亲手死去的 极富创造力的头脑,你知道吗?

sentences.en: And even the ones who didn't literally commit suicide seem to be really undone by their gifts, you know.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些没有真正自杀的人 似乎真的被他们的天赋所摧毁了

sentences.en: Norman Mailer, just before he died, last interview, he said, "Every one of my books has killed me a little more."
sentences.zh: 诺曼·梅勒 死前的最后一次采访 他说 "我的每本书都让我更难受"

sentences.en: An extraordinary statement to make about your life's work.
sentences.zh: 一个非凡的声明 对你的生活的工作。

sentences.en: But we don't even blink when we hear somebody say this, because we've heard that kind of stuff for so long and somehow we've completely internalized and accepted collectively this notion that creativity and suffering are somehow inherently linked
sentences.zh: 但是我们甚至不眨眼 当我们听到有人说, 因为我们听到这种东西 这么久, 不知怎的,我们完全内部化 并集体接受这个概念 即创造力和痛苦 某种程度上是相互联系的

sentences.en: and that artistry, in the end, will always ultimately lead to anguish.
sentences.zh: 艺术家最终将最终导致痛苦。

sentences.en: And the question that I want to ask everybody here today is are you guys all cool with that idea?
sentences.zh: 今天我想问大家的问题是 你们都同意这个想法吗?

sentences.en: Are you comfortable with that? Because you look at it even from an inch away and, you know -- I'm not at all comfortable with that assumption.
sentences.zh: 你同意吗?因为你甚至从一寸以外看它,而且,你知道—— 我对那个假设完全不满意。

sentences.en: I think it's odious. And I also think it's dangerous, and I don't want to see it perpetuated into the next century.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很恶心,我也觉得很危险 我不想看到它持续到下个世纪

sentences.en: I think it's better if we encourage our great creative minds to live.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们最好鼓励我们伟大的创意思想生活

sentences.en: And I definitely know that, in my case -- in my situation -- it would be very dangerous for me to start sort of leaking down that dark path of assumption,
sentences.zh: 我绝对知道,在我的情况下—— 在我的处境下—— 我开始从黑暗的假设中泄漏出去会非常危险,

sentences.en: particularly given the circumstance that I'm in right now in my career.
sentences.zh: 特别是考虑到我现在的处境

sentences.en: Which is -- you know, like check it out, I'm pretty young, I'm only about 40 years old.
sentences.zh: 也就是说,你知道,像检查出来一样, 我年轻,我只有40岁左右。

sentences.en: I still have maybe another four decades of work left in me.
sentences.zh: 我还有四十年的工作

sentences.en: And it's exceedingly likely that anything I write from this point forward is going to be judged by the world as the work that came after the freakish success of my last book, right?
sentences.zh: 我写的任何东西 很可能都会被世界评为 我最后一本书成功后的工作,对吧?

sentences.en: I should just put it bluntly, because we're all sort of friends here now -- it's exceedingly likely that my greatest success is behind me.
sentences.zh: 我应该直截了当地说, 因为我们现在都是朋友了—— 我最伟大的成功很可能在我身后。

sentences.en: So Jesus, what a thought! That's the kind of thought that could lead a person to start drinking gin at nine o'clock in the morning, and I don't want to go there.
sentences.zh: 所以,耶稣,多么的想法! 那种想法可以引导一个人 开始喝酒 在早上9点, 我不想去那里。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I would prefer to keep doing this work that I love.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 我宁愿继续做这份我爱的工作。

sentences.en: And so, the question becomes, how? And so, it seems to me, upon a lot of reflection, that the way that I have to work now, in order to continue writing, is that I have to create some sort of protective psychological construct, right?
sentences.zh: 所以,问题变成了怎样?所以,在我看来,从很多的反省来看,我现在的工作方式, 为了继续写作, 是要创造某种保护性心理结构,对吧?

sentences.en: I have to sort of find some way to have a safe distance between me, as I am writing, and my very natural anxiety about what the reaction to that writing is going to be, from now on.
sentences.zh: 我必须找到某种方法 保持我之间的安全距离, 当我正在写作, 和我非常自然的焦虑 对于什么 反应该写作是 未来,从现在开始。

sentences.en: And, as I've been looking, over the last year, for models for how to do that, I've been sort of looking across time, and I've been trying to find other societies to see if they might have had better and saner ideas than we have
sentences.zh: 和,我一直在寻找,在过去的一年, 模型如何做到这一点, 我一直在寻找 一种时间,我一直在寻找 其它的社会,

sentences.en: about how to help creative people sort of manage the inherent emotional risks of creativity.
sentences.zh: 如何帮助有创造力的人 管理创造力的内在情感风险。

sentences.en: And that search has led me to ancient Greece and ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 搜索让我来到了古希腊和古罗马

sentences.en: So stay with me, because it does circle around and back.
sentences.zh: 所以留在我身边 因为它会绕圈子绕回来

sentences.en: But, ancient Greece and ancient Rome -- people did not happen to believe that creativity came from human beings back then, OK?
sentences.zh: 但是,古希腊和古罗马 人们并不认为 创造力来自人类,好吗?

sentences.en: People believed that creativity was this divine attendant spirit that came to human beings from some distant and unknowable source, for distant and unknowable reasons.
sentences.zh: 人们相信,创造力是人类从遥远和未知的源头、由于遥远和未知的原因传到人类身上的神圣精神。

sentences.en: The Greeks famously called these divine attendant spirits of creativity "daemons."
sentences.zh: 希腊人将这些神圣的创造力伴随灵魂称为“恶魔”。

sentences.en: Socrates, famously, believed that he had a daemon who spoke wisdom to him from afar.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，苏格拉底相信他有一个恶魔从远处向他讲授智慧。

sentences.en: The Romans had the same idea, but they called that sort of disembodied creative spirit a genius.
sentences.zh: 罗马人也有同样的想法，但他们把这种无形的创造精神称为天才。

sentences.en: Which is great, because the Romans did not actually think that a genius was a particularly clever individual.
sentences.zh: 这很好，因为罗马人实际上并不认为天才是一个特别聪明的人。

sentences.en: They believed that a genius was this, sort of magical divine entity, who was believed to literally live in the walls of an artist's studio, kind of like Dobby the house elf, and who would come out
sentences.zh: 他们相信天才就是这样一种神奇的神圣实体，人们相信他实际上生活在艺术家工作室的墙壁里，有点像家养小精灵多比，并且他会出来

sentences.en: and sort of invisibly assist the artist with their work and would shape the outcome of that work.
sentences.zh: 并在无形中帮助艺术家完成他们的工作，并塑造该作品的结果。

sentences.en: So brilliant -- there it is, right there, that distance that I'm talking about -- that psychological construct to protect you from the results of your work.
sentences.zh: 太棒了——就在那里，就在那里，我所说的距离——保护你免受工作结果影响的心理结构。

sentences.en: And everyone knew that this is how it functioned, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道它是这样运作的，对吧？

sentences.en: So the ancient artist was protected from certain things, like, for example, too much narcissism, right?
sentences.zh: 所以古代艺术家受到了保护，免受某些事情的影响，例如过度自恋，对吧？

sentences.en: If your work was brilliant, you couldn't take all the credit for it, everybody knew that you had this disembodied genius who had helped you.
sentences.zh: 如果你的工作很出色，你就不能把所有的功劳都归功于你，每个人都知道你有一个无形的天才帮助过你。

sentences.en: If your work bombed, not entirely your fault, you know?
sentences.zh: 如果你的工作失败了，这并不完全是你的错，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knew your genius was kind of lame.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你的天才有点蹩脚。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And this is how people thought about creativity in the West for a really long time.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 这就是西方人长期以来对创造力的看法。

sentences.en: And then the Renaissance came and everything changed, and we had this big idea, and the big idea was, let's put the individual human being at the center of the universe above all gods and mysteries, and there's no more room for mystical creatures
sentences.zh: 然后文艺复兴到来了，一切都改变了，我们有了这个伟大的想法，这个伟大的想法是，让我们把个体人类置于宇宙的中心，高于所有的神灵和神秘事物，不再有神秘生物的空间

sentences.en: who take dictation from the divine. And it's the beginning of rational humanism, and people started to believe that creativity came completely from the self of the individual.
sentences.zh: 他们接受神的口授。这是理性人文主义的开始，人们开始相信创造力完全来自个人的自我。

sentences.en: And for the first time in history, you start to hear people referring to this or that artist as being a genius, rather than having a genius.
sentences.zh: 历史上第一次，你开始听到人们称这个或那个艺术家为天才，而不是拥有天才。

sentences.en: And I got to tell you, I think that was a huge error.
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，我认为这是一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: You know, I think that allowing somebody, one mere person to believe that he or she is like, the vessel, you know, like the font and the essence and the source of all divine, creative, unknowable, eternal mystery
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为让某人，一个单纯的人相信他或她就像一个容器，你知道，就像所有神圣的、创造性的、不可知的、永恒的奥秘的字体、本质和源泉

sentences.en: is just a smidge too much responsibility to put on one fragile, human psyche.
sentences.zh: 对于一个脆弱的人类心灵来说，责任有点太大了。

sentences.en: It's like asking somebody to swallow the sun.
sentences.zh: 这就像要求某人吞下太阳一样。

sentences.en: It just completely warps and distorts egos, and it creates all these unmanageable expectations about performance.
sentences.zh: 它完全扭曲了自我，并且创造了所有这些对绩效难以管理的期望。

sentences.en: And I think the pressure of that has been killing off our artists for the last 500 years.
sentences.zh: 我认为过去 500 年来这种压力一直在扼杀我们的艺术家。

sentences.en: And, if this is true, and I think it is true, the question becomes, what now?
sentences.zh: 而且，如果这是真的，而且我认为这是真的，那么问题就变成了，现在怎么办？

sentences.en: Can we do this differently? Maybe go back to some more ancient understanding about the relationship between humans and the creative mystery.
sentences.zh: 我们可以采取不同的做法吗？也许可以回到一些更古老的关于人类与创造性之谜之间的关系的理解。

sentences.en: Maybe not. Maybe we can't just erase 500 years of rational humanistic thought in one 18 minute speech.
sentences.zh: 也许不是。也许我们不能在一次18分钟的演讲中就抹掉500年的理性人文思想。

sentences.en: And there's probably people in this audience who would raise really legitimate scientific suspicions about the notion of, basically, fairies who follow people around rubbing fairy juice on their projects and stuff.
sentences.zh: 也许在座的观众会提出 真正的科学怀疑 基本上,是仙子们的观念 跟随人们在他们的项目和东西上 摩擦仙子汁

sentences.en: I'm not, probably, going to bring you all along with me on this.
sentences.zh: 我可能不会 带你和我一起参与这件事

sentences.en: But the question that I kind of want to pose is -- you know, why not?
sentences.zh: 但我想提出的问题是-- 为什么不呢?

sentences.en: Why not think about it this way? Because it makes as much sense as anything else I have ever heard in terms of explaining the utter maddening capriciousness of the creative process.
sentences.zh: 为什么不这样想呢? 因为它和我听到的其他任何声音一样有意义,它解释了创造性进程的极端疯狂的反复无常。

sentences.en: A process which, as anybody who has ever tried to make something -- which is to say basically everyone here --- knows does not always behave rationally.
sentences.zh: 一个过程,作为任何曾经试图做一些事情 -- -- 也就是说基本上每个人都知道 -- -- 并不总能理性地行事。

sentences.en: And, in fact, can sometimes feel downright paranormal.
sentences.zh: 而且,事实上,有时可以感觉 直接的超自然现象。

sentences.en: I had this encounter recently where I met the extraordinary American poet Ruth Stone, who's now in her 90s, but she's been a poet her entire life and she told me that when she was growing up in rural Virginia, she would be out working in the fields,
sentences.zh: 我最近遇到一位杰出的美国诗人露丝·斯通, 她现在在90年代, 但她一生都是一位诗人, 她告诉我,当她在弗吉尼亚州农村长大时, 她将会在田里工作,

sentences.en: and she said she would feel and hear a poem coming at her from over the landscape.
sentences.zh: 她说,她会感觉 并听到一首诗 来从她的地貌。

sentences.en: And she said it was like a thunderous train of air.
sentences.zh: 她说这就像一列雷电般的空气

sentences.en: And it would come barreling down at her over the landscape.
sentences.zh: 就会在地表上冲向她

sentences.en: And she felt it coming, because it would shake the earth under her feet.
sentences.zh: 她感觉到它的到来, 因为它会摇动大地 在她的脚下。

sentences.en: She knew that she had only one thing to do at that point, and that was to, in her words, "run like hell."
sentences.zh: 她知道当时她只有一件事要做 用她的话来说 "跑得像地狱"

sentences.en: And she would run like hell to the house and she would be getting chased by this poem, and the whole deal was that she had to get to a piece of paper and a pencil fast enough so that when it thundered through her, she could collect it
sentences.zh: 她会跑得像地狱 房子,她会被追 被这首诗, 整个交易是 她得到一块纸和铅笔 足够快,这样当它打通她, 她可以收集它

sentences.en: and grab it on the page. And other times she wouldn't be fast enough, so she'd be running and running, and she wouldn't get to the house and the poem would barrel through her and she would miss it and she said it would continue on across the landscape,
sentences.zh: 有时她跑得不够快,所以她跑得不够快, 连这首诗都弹不出来, 她会错过,说会一直传遍整个地貌,

sentences.en: looking, as she put it "for another poet."
sentences.zh: 看着,正如她所说的 "为另一个诗人。"

sentences.en: And then there were these times -- this is the piece I never forgot -- she said that there were moments where she would almost miss it, right?
sentences.zh: 然后有这些时候,这就是我从未忘记的, 她说有些时候,她几乎会错过,对吗?

sentences.en: So, she's running to the house and she's looking for the paper and the poem passes through her, and she grabs a pencil just as it's going through her, and then she said, it was like she would reach out with her other hand
sentences.zh: 所以,她跑到 房子,她寻找 报纸和诗通过她, 她抓住铅笔 因为它正在穿过她, 然后她说,

sentences.en: and she would catch it. She would catch the poem by its tail, and she would pull it backwards into her body as she was transcribing on the page.
sentences.zh: 她会抓住它。她会抓住它的尾巴, 她会把它拉回她的身体, 当她在页面上转录。

sentences.en: And in these instances, the poem would come up on the page perfect and intact but backwards, from the last word to the first.
sentences.zh: 在这些例子中, 诗会出现在页面上 完美和完整 但倒过来, 从最后一句话到第一个字。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So when I heard that I was like -- that's uncanny, that's exactly what my creative process is like.
sentences.zh: 所以当我听到我像 - 这是不可思议的, 这正是我的创造过程是什么样子。

sentences.en: (Laughter) That's not at all what my creative process is -- I'm not the pipeline!
sentences.zh: (笑声) 这根本不是我的创造过程- 我不是管道!

sentences.en: I'm a mule, and the way that I have to work is I have to get up at the same time every day, and sweat and labor and barrel through it really awkwardly.
sentences.zh: 我是一个骡子,我的工作方式是 每天我必须同时起床, 汗水和劳动力 和桶穿它真的很尴尬。

sentences.en: But even I, in my mulishness, even I have brushed up against that thing, at times.
sentences.zh: 但是,即使我,在我的默默无闻, 甚至我梳了起来 与那东西,有时。

sentences.en: And I would imagine that a lot of you have too.
sentences.zh: 我会想象你们中的很多人也有

sentences.en: You know, even I have had work or ideas come through me from a source that I honestly cannot identify.
sentences.zh: 你知道,即使我有工作或想法 从我无法真正识别的来源。

sentences.en: And what is that thing? And how are we to relate to it in a way that will not make us lose our minds, but, in fact, might actually keep us sane?
sentences.zh: 那东西是什么？我们如何以一种既不会让我们失去理智，又能让我们保持理智的方式来对待它？

sentences.en: And for me, the best contemporary example that I have of how to do that is the musician Tom Waits, who I got to interview several years ago on a magazine assignment.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，当代最好的例子就是音乐家汤姆·威茨（Tom Waits），几年前我在一份杂志任务中采访了他。

sentences.en: And we were talking about this, and you know, Tom, for most of his life, he was pretty much the embodiment of the tormented contemporary modern artist, trying to control and manage and dominate these sort of uncontrollable creative impulses
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论这个，你知道，汤姆，在他一生的大部分时间里，他几乎是饱受折磨的当代现代艺术家的化身，试图控制、管理和支配这些无法控制的创作冲动

sentences.en: that were totally internalized. But then he got older, he got calmer, and one day he was driving down the freeway in Los Angeles, and this is when it all changed for him.
sentences.zh: 那些已经完全内化了。但随着年龄的增长，他变得更加平静，有一天，他开车沿着洛杉矶的高速公路行驶，从那时起，一切都改变了。

sentences.en: And he's speeding along, and all of a sudden he hears this little fragment of melody, that comes into his head as inspiration often comes, elusive and tantalizing, and he wants it, it's gorgeous, and he longs for it, but he has no way to get it.
sentences.zh: 他正在飞快地前行，突然他听到了这个小片段的旋律，当灵感经常出现时，它就会进入他的脑海，难以捉摸，诱人，他想要它，它很华丽，他渴望它，但他没有办法得到它。

sentences.en: He doesn't have a piece of paper, or a pencil, or a tape recorder.
sentences.zh: 他没有一张纸，一支铅笔，或者一台录音机。

sentences.en: So he starts to feel all of that old anxiety start to rise in him like, "I'm going to lose this thing, and I'll be haunted by this song forever.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始感到所有旧有的焦虑开始在他体内升起，就像，“我将失去这件事，我将永远被这首歌所困扰。

sentences.en: I'm not good enough, and I can't do it."
sentences.zh: 我不够好，我做不到。”

sentences.en: And instead of panicking, he just stopped.
sentences.zh: 他并没有惊慌，而是停了下来。

sentences.en: He just stopped that whole mental process and he did something completely novel.
sentences.zh: 他只是停止了整个心理过程，做了一些完全新颖的事情。

sentences.en: He just looked up at the sky, and he said, "Excuse me, can you not see that I'm driving?"
sentences.zh: 他只是抬头看着天空，说道：“请问，你没看到我正在开车吗？”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "Do I look like I can write down a song right now?
sentences.zh: （笑声）“我看起来像现在就能写歌吗？

sentences.en: If you really want to exist, come back at a more opportune moment when I can take care of you.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想存在的话，就等我可以照顾你的时候回来吧。

sentences.en: Otherwise, go bother somebody else today.
sentences.zh: 不然今天就去麻烦别人了。

sentences.en: Go bother Leonard Cohen." And his whole work process changed after that.
sentences.zh: 去打扰莱昂纳德·科恩吧。”此后他的整个工作流程发生了变化。

sentences.en: Not the work, the work was still oftentimes as dark as ever.
sentences.zh: 不是工作，而是工作常常仍然像以前一样黑暗。

sentences.en: But the process, and the heavy anxiety around it was released when he took the genie, the genius out of him where it was causing nothing but trouble, and released it back where it came from, and realized that this didn't have to be this internalized, tormented thing.
sentences.zh: 但当他把那个只会给他带来麻烦的精灵、天才从他身上拿走，然后把它放回它原来的地方时，这个过程以及围绕它的沉重焦虑就被释放了，并意识到这不一定是这种内化的、折磨人的东西。

sentences.en: It could be this peculiar, wondrous, bizarre collaboration, kind of conversation between Tom and the strange, external thing that was not quite Tom.
sentences.zh: 这可能是汤姆和那个不完全是汤姆的奇怪的、外在的东西之间的这种奇特、奇妙、奇异的合作，一种对话。

sentences.en: When I heard that story, it started to shift a little bit the way that I worked too, and this idea already saved me once.
sentences.zh: 当我听到这个故事时，我的工作方式也开始发生一些改变，这个想法已经救了我一次。

sentences.en: It saved me when I was in the middle of writing "Eat, Pray, Love," and I fell into one of those sort of pits of despair that we all fall into when we're working on something and it's not coming and you start to think this is going to be a disaster, the worst book ever written.
sentences.zh: 当我正在写《美食、祈祷、爱情》的时候，它救了我，我陷入了一种绝望的深渊，当我们在做某件事而它没有到来时，我们都会陷入这种绝望的深渊，你开始认为这将是一场灾难，是有史以来最糟糕的书。

sentences.en: Not just bad, but the worst book ever written.
sentences.zh: 不仅糟糕，而且是有史以来最糟糕的书。

sentences.en: And I started to think I should just dump this project.
sentences.zh: 我开始想我应该放弃这个项目。

sentences.en: But then I remembered Tom talking to the open air and I tried it.
sentences.zh: 但后来我想起汤姆在露天说话，我就尝试了。

sentences.en: So I just lifted my face up from the manuscript and I directed my comments to an empty corner of the room.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是把脸从手稿上抬起来，然后把我的评论指向房间的一个空角落。

sentences.en: And I said aloud, "Listen you, thing, you and I both know that if this book isn't brilliant that is not entirely my fault, right?
sentences.zh: 我大声说道：“听着，你和我都知道，如果这本书不精彩，那也不完全是我的错，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you can see that I am putting everything I have into this, I don't have any more than this.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以看到,我把 我的一切在这里, 我没有什么比这更多。

sentences.en: If you want it to be better, you've got to show up and do your part of the deal.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要更好, 你必须出现 并做你的一部分交易。

sentences.en: But if you don't do that, you know what, the hell with it.
sentences.zh: 但是,如果你不这样做, 你知道什么,地狱与它。

sentences.en: I'm going to keep writing anyway because that's my job.
sentences.zh: 反正我会继续写 因为我的工作。

sentences.en: And I would please like the record to reflect today that I showed up for my part of the job."
sentences.zh: 我希望记录今天能反映 我为我的工作所做的部分。"

sentences.en: (Laughter) Because -- (Applause) Because in the end it's like this, OK -- centuries ago in the deserts of North Africa, people used to gather for these moonlight dances of sacred dance and music
sentences.zh: (笑声) 因为- (掌声) 因为最后,这是这样的,OK- 几个世纪前在北非的沙漠里, 人们用来聚集 这些月光舞蹈 神圣的舞蹈和音乐

sentences.en: that would go on for hours and hours, until dawn.
sentences.zh: 它会持续几个小时,直到黎明。

sentences.en: They were always magnificent, because the dancers were professionals and they were terrific, right?
sentences.zh: 舞者们都很专业,很了不起,对吧?

sentences.en: But every once in a while, very rarely, something would happen, and one of these performers would actually become transcendent.
sentences.zh: 但偶尔 很少会发生一些事情 其中一个表演者会变得超凡

sentences.en: And I know you know what I'm talking about, because I know you've all seen, at some point in your life, a performance like this.
sentences.zh: 我知道你知道我在说什么, 因为我知道你们都见过, 在你们生活中的某个时刻, 像这样的表演。

sentences.en: It was like time would stop, and the dancer would sort of step through some kind of portal and he wasn't doing anything different than he had ever done, 1,000 nights before, but everything would align.
sentences.zh: 这就像时间会停止, 舞者会排序 通过某种门户 和他没有做 任何不同,他以前做过, 1000晚前, 但一切都会一致。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, he would no longer appear to be merely human.
sentences.zh: 突然间,他不再只是个人类

sentences.en: He would be lit from within, and lit from below and all lit up on fire with divinity.
sentences.zh: 他从里面被点燃,从下面被点燃,然后,他用精华点燃。

sentences.en: And when this happened, back then, people knew it for what it was, you know, they called it by its name.
sentences.zh: 当这件事发生的时候, 那时,人们知道它是什么, 你知道,他们把它叫做它的名字。

sentences.en: They would put their hands together and they would start to chant, "Allah, Allah, God, God."
sentences.zh: 他们把双手放在一起 开始高喊: "真主,真主,上帝,上帝"

sentences.en: That's God, you know. Curious historical footnote: when the Moors invaded southern Spain, they took this custom with them and the pronunciation changed over the centuries
sentences.zh: 这是上帝,你知道。奇怪的历史脚注:当摩尔人入侵西班牙南部时, 他们采取了这个习俗, 和发音变化了几个世纪

sentences.en: from "Allah, Allah, Allah," to "Olé, olé, olé," which you still hear in bullfights and in flamenco dances.
sentences.zh: 从"真主,真主,真主"到"奥莱,奥莱,奥莱,奥莱" 你仍然听到在斗牛和火焰舞。

sentences.en: In Spain, when a performer has done something impossible and magic, "Allah, olé, Allah, magnificent, bravo," incomprehensible, there it is -- a glimpse of God.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙,当一个表演者做了一些不可能的事和魔术的时候, “真主,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的,万能的。

sentences.en: Which is great, because we need that. But, the tricky bit comes the next morning, for the dancer himself, when he wakes up and discovers that it's Tuesday at 11 a.m., and he's no longer a glimpse of God.
sentences.zh: 这很好,因为我们需要这一点。但是,第二天早晨, 舞者自己, 当他醒来发现这是星期二上午11点, 他不再是上帝的一瞥。

sentences.en: He's just an aging mortal with really bad knees, and maybe he's never going to ascend to that height again.
sentences.zh: 他只是个年老的凡人 膝盖真的不好, 也许他永远不会 升到那个高度了。

sentences.en: And maybe nobody will ever chant God's name again as he spins, and what is he then to do with the rest of his life?
sentences.zh: 也许没有人会再高呼上帝的名字 当他转动时, 然后他要怎么处理他的余生?

sentences.en: This is hard. This is one of the most painful reconciliations to make in a creative life.
sentences.zh: 这是很难的,这是在创造性生活中最痛苦的和解之一。

sentences.en: But maybe it doesn't have to be quite so full of anguish if you never happened to believe, in the first place, that the most extraordinary aspects of your being came from you.
sentences.zh: 但也许它不一定要 相当充满痛苦 如果你从来没有碰巧相信, 首先,你最非凡的方面 来自于你。

sentences.en: But maybe if you just believed that they were on loan to you from some unimaginable source for some exquisite portion of your life to be passed along when you're finished, with somebody else.
sentences.zh: 但也许你只是相信 他们是借给你的 从一些难以想象的来源

sentences.en: And, you know, if we think about it this way, it starts to change everything.
sentences.zh: 而且,你知道,如果我们这样想, 它开始改变一切。

sentences.en: This is how I've started to think, and this is certainly how I've been thinking in the last few months as I've been working on the book that will soon be published, as the dangerously, frighteningly over-anticipated follow up
sentences.zh: 这就是我开始的想法, 并且这肯定是我在过去几个月里的想法, 因为我一直在写一本很快会出版的书, 作为危险的, 令人惊恐的, 过分期待的后续行动

sentences.en: to my freakish success. And what I have to sort of keep telling myself when I get really psyched out about that is don't be afraid.
sentences.zh: 我不得不不停地告诉自己 当我被迷惑的时候

sentences.en: Don't be daunted. Just do your job. Continue to show up for your piece of it, whatever that might be.
sentences.zh: 别害怕 做好你的工作 继续为你的工作出面 不管是什么

sentences.en: If your job is to dance, do your dance. If the divine, cockeyed genius assigned to your case decides to let some sort of wonderment be glimpsed, for just one moment through your efforts, then "Olé!"
sentences.zh: 如果你的工作是跳舞,就跳你的舞。 如果你案子的神明的天才决定让一些奇观被窥视。

sentences.en: And if not, do your dance anyhow. And "Olé!" to you, nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 如果没有,就跳你的舞吧,还有"奥莱"

sentences.en: I believe this and I feel that we must teach it.
sentences.zh: 我相信这一点,我觉得我们必须教它。

sentences.en: "Olé!" to you, nonetheless, just for having the sheer human love and stubbornness to keep showing up.
sentences.zh: "Olé!" 对你,尽管如此, 仅仅因为有人类的爱 和固执 不断出现。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause) Thank you. (Applause) June Cohen: Olé!
sentences.zh: 谢谢。 (掌声) 谢谢。 (掌声)

sentences.en: (Applause)
sentences.zh: （掌声）
